learnTa.title: Learn technical analysis
learnTa.intro: A reference for the indicators on the markets page. Each section explains when an indicator is the right tool, how to configure it, and how to read its signals — with curated links to dig deeper.
learnTa.buySellSubtitle: Turning indicator signals into decisions — with market regime, fundamentals, news, and risk management as the context around the chart.
learnTa.paletteSummary: The core Finatalk indicators and the extended families of substitutes and confirmations.
learnTa.coreIndicatorsIntro: These are the five indicators highlighted by default in Finatalk. The families below show substitutes and confirmations you can add next.

learnInvestment.title: Learn investment
learnInvestment.intro: A practical reference to the main investment types available to Québec/Canadian investors — from a bank savings account to a fund of funds. For each, you'll find characteristics, when and why to buy, and how profits are paid and taxed in Québec.
learnInvestment.disclaimer: Educational content — not investment, tax, or legal advice. Rates and tax figures reflect the 2025 Québec/Canada framework and may change. Consult a qualified advisor for your personal situation.
learnInvestment.howToBuy: Where and how to buy it

learnFees.title: Investment fees
learnFees.intro: Every dollar you pay in fees is a dollar that doesn't compound for your future. This is a complete reference to every fee a Canadian retail investor encounters — commissions, MER, trailers, FX, admin, transfer, advisor — with typical costs and how to minimize each one.
learnFees.disclaimer: Educational content — not investment, tax, or legal advice. Fee schedules change; always verify current rates with your broker before acting. Ranges reflect the 2025 Canadian retail market.

learnRates.title: Analyse rates
learnRates.intro: A guide to reading the Rates dashboard and translating yield curves, spreads, and central-bank policy rates into concrete investment decisions. Covers both US and Canadian context, with a focus on what Canadian retail investors can act on.
learnRates.disclaimer: Educational content — not investment, tax, or legal advice. Rate regimes evolve; re-read the data on the Rates page before acting. Consult a qualified advisor for your personal situation.
learnRates.investorAction: What to do as an investor

learnStrategies.title: Investment strategies
learnStrategies.intro: A reference guide to well-known investment strategies for buying, holding, and selling stocks, bonds, and funds. Each section explains how the strategy works, when to use it, and its strengths and weaknesses — with a Canadian/Quebec perspective where applicable.
learnStrategies.disclaimer: Educational content — not investment, tax, or legal advice. Past performance of any strategy does not guarantee future results. Consult a qualified advisor for your personal situation.

backtest.title: Strategy backtest
backtest.intro: Run one of the documented strategies against historical bars and see how the signals would have played out. Uses next-open entries, ATR-based stops, a fixed take-profit multiple of R, and transaction-fee + slippage assumptions. Educational only — past performance does not guarantee future results.
backtest.phase1Note: Phase 1: daily bars, long-only, single-position, one strategy at a time.
backtest.phase2Note: Phase 2: intraday intervals, short-side trades, buy & hold benchmark overlay, parameter sweeps, and multi-asset portfolios.

sweep.title: Parameter sweep
sweep.hint: Run a grid of backtests across two parameters and view the chosen metric as a heatmap.
sweep.samePairError: X and Y must use different parameters.
sweep.tooBigError: Grid too large — keep cell count at or below 64.

portfolio.reviewPrompt: Do a full rebalance review of this portfolio. For EACH holding, pull the current price, RSI 14, MACD, SMA 50 and SMA 200 trend, ADX, analyst consensus target and recommendation, and the latest headlines. Then label the holding HOLD, TRIM, or REPLACE with a one-sentence rationale citing the numbers. If REPLACE, suggest 1–2 concrete alternative tickers in the same sector/theme. End with a short portfolio-level note on concentration, sector gaps, and cash drag.
